findings.explanation: The root explicitly links its three components under relative paths. Following root → data/raw_eyegaze → .gitmodules exposes a source dependency with a machine-local URL. Partial is defensible for the declared recursive scope; it must remain qualified as an upstream provenance-boundary defect, not missing curated paper inputs.

The recorded paper inputs are rooted in its module tree, while the explicitly linked raw-data source has only a local URL. This is a concrete recursive exception supporting partial without a network experiment. The assessment correctly avoids treating absent payloads as failed retrievals.

The linked REMoDNaV source and scientific dependencies are represented within the root by gitlinks and the Docker recipe, and the label component links its own REMoDNaV version. Met on software inclusion is reasonable; this does not establish that the historical label environment is pinned or that its obsolete Condor instructions work.

The frozen Git tree supplies object identities for code, configuration and manuscript text. Deliberately omitted payload files in an inspection checkout cannot show that committed project sources lack version control. The override of the checkout-cleanliness heuristic is warranted.

The image and studyforrest annex pointers clearly support large-payload versioning for those components. However, linked Anderson binary payloads are ordinary Git blobs, and offline ls-tree returned unknown sizes for 176 and 175 omitted blobs in its two linked revisions. Git identity alone does not settle the native probe’s large-binary criterion. This leaves the all-component met insufficiently verified; it does not establish a violation.
findings.suggested_correction: State the verified annex coverage and the unresolved Anderson size/storage coverage. Obtain a frozen size inventory or otherwise justify why the linked binary blobs satisfy this property before retaining an unqualified met.

findings.explanation: The paper record includes container/image as extra_inputs and declares img and results_def.tex as outputs. The label record runs bash code/compute_all.sh with no environment capture. Partial follows from this concrete contrast. The assessment also correctly rejects the probe coverage count as proof of complete provenance.

Installation and usage text exists, and the root accurately labels its legacy route. However, rule 10 also requires comparing instructions with the actual mechanism: the root promises recomputation of every numerical value while its dispatched functions omit quality_stats; the linked README names removed preprocessing/detection scripts rather than the recorded compute_all.sh route. These are additional conflicts, not the honestly disclosed container migration.
findings.suggested_correction: Change met to partial, retaining the correct override of the spurious make-changes probe finding and adding the independently verified instruction/mechanism conflicts.

findings.explanation: The named rerun is a real starting point, but Docker-Makefile invokes only -s -f -r -m. The CLI never calls quality_stats, whose docstring explicitly says it must be added to the invocation list; main.tex reports 15.1% and 4.1% signal loss. Thus the documented all-numerical-results route has a demonstrated coverage gap. Native rule 10 caps the judgment at partial when documentation and mechanism disagree.
findings.suggested_correction: Change met to partial and name the omitted signal-loss calculation. Distinguish a usable starting point from complete coverage of the documented scope.

findings.explanation: The linked submission scripts contain fixed user-directory and interpreter paths. These are actual host assumptions, unlike cleanup paths inside the Debian image. Partial appropriately reflects the root relative-path workflow together with the legacy linked-script violations.

The root recipe specifies its scientific/rendering packages, but the recorded label workflow invokes the caller Python and inherits PYTHONPATH without reconstructing an environment. This concrete component gap supports partial. Lack of a complete host lockfile alone would be a weaker rationale than the missing label execution environment.

Supported operating systems and Docker versions are described at the root. Following the label module reveals undocumented directory/interpreter/environment inheritance. The Docker adapter also assumes a usable non-root Docker executable. Partial is supported without requiring execution on additional hosts.

The root supplies a substantial requirements list, while the label README gives old Condor commands and no requirements matching its current recorded Python route. The package setup metadata lists Python libraries but does not repair the linked reproduction instructions; partial is justified.

The relevant specifications that exist are versioned: recipe, registration, archive manifest and linked package dependency metadata. Met addresses their tracking; incompleteness and historical exactness belong to must/010 and must/015 rather than making these tracked files untracked.

The build record supplies an executable rebuild/save procedure, and the later OCI conversion is a separate recorded maintenance action responding to Docker compatibility. This is more than counting the introduction of a file as an update. Met is reasonable for the paper environment, and the duplicate flag matches the native protocol.

The root archive is content-pinned; the adapter hashes its saved configuration and executes the resulting image ID, so RepoTags latest is not a floating execution selector. But the declared assessment scope includes label generation, whose Python/scientific-library environment has neither a frozen manifest nor an archived image. Met across the object contradicts the same assessment’s supported environment gaps under must/006 and must/010.
findings.suggested_correction: Change met to partial: retain the pinned paper-image strength and explicitly identify the unpinned linked label environment. Cite the adapter using its frozen digest or a commit-pinned URL rather than only a version-tag URL.

findings.explanation: The frozen recipe and annex availability records establish a publication mechanism, but do not demonstrate present retrieval of the archived environment bytes. Not-checked is a defensible conservative result under the prohibited-network boundary. It correctly preserves the unknown rather than asserting a distribution failure.

The root clearly explains acquisition and use of docker-make, but the explicitly included label computation has no matching environment acquisition/use instructions: its README leads to the old Condor pipeline while history records compute_all.sh. An all-object met applies a narrower boundary here than under must/010–012 and should/005.
findings.suggested_correction: Use partial for the stated recursive scope, citing the adequate root instructions and the missing current label-environment instructions separately.

findings.explanation: All discovered components are composed through Git identities; annex supplements Git for large payloads. The root’s nested gitlinks, including separate REMoDNaV versions, support a common version-control mechanism without needing payload retrieval.

The tool CI definition exercises installation and pytest, while the paper has a historical recomputation record rather than a regular full-study instruction test. Partial credits component-level automated checks and historical maintenance without upgrading a workflow definition to an observed successful current run.

The root separates raw input, label derivatives, algorithm source, image directory and figure outputs; the label component likewise separates input modules from code and subject outputs. These are meaningful component boundaries even though not every output directory is its own repository.

The exit-zero record executes the analysis through the Docker adapter; its inspected cli_run builds a docker run invocation with --rm. This is committed equivalent evidence of a fresh-container paper recomputation, allowed by the native method. It is not an observed new run, nor evidence that the upstream label generation was isolated.

The paper route creates a disposable Docker container and temporary HOME. The label route uses the caller Python with inherited PYTHONPATH and no per-run environment creation. Partial follows directly from the two execution mechanisms, not merely from missing execution logs.

The archived environment was exercised during recomputation and later loaded/run for OCI maintenance. The tool CI installs a different dependency set and cannot establish regular recreation of the paper image. Partial reasonably credits demonstrated maintenance while leaving the recurring full-environment guarantee unsatisfied.

The image config/layers are represented inside the research-object tree with annex content identities, and the README explains obtaining the archive. That establishes archived artifact structure; absent payloads in this evidence package do not disprove archiving. Current retrievability remains the separate unknown in must/016.

This is the exact duplicate of must/014. The same executable build procedure and later recorded compatibility maintenance support the same judgment, and both responses correctly carry upstream-duplicate.

The raw-data documentation explicitly declares unrestricted access and no authentication. No restricted component is identified in the discovered paper inputs. The native empty-subject rule supports not-applicable; a machine-local source URL is not evidence of a restriction policy.

External raw data, labels, REMoDNaV and Anderson data are explicit nested modules. This criterion asks whether links exist, so the inaccessible local upstream source URL does not negate the module-linking property.

The root gives useful roles and a reproduction route, but the linked label README does not connect its raw-data and REMoDNaV modules to the computation actually recorded in history. Partial is supported by a concrete documentation gap in the recursive structure.

The evidence shows independent pinned components and historical dependency drift, but does not isolate a defect in the module boundaries themselves. A dependency API changing and a README being stale do not by themselves establish that the boundaries prevent independent updates. The current partial rationale therefore mixes portability/documentation issues with the criterion’s boundary property.
findings.suggested_correction: Either identify a concrete coupling or replacement that requires changes outside its module, or revise the rationale/status to reflect the inspected structural evidence and state that safe recombination was not demonstrated by an execution test.

findings.explanation: Gitlinks define composition and DataLad’s recorded input/output paths connect those modules to the registered image and Make targets. This is a concrete composition mechanism even where separate criteria find incomplete environment history or instructions.

Module paths and repositories are navigable from the root, but navigating into the label README leads to obsolete commands rather than the recorded production route. Partial distinguishes usable root navigation from this demonstrated linked-component documentation problem.

limitations: Inspection-only review of frozen cohort remodnav-e3c6253bced7; manifest SHA256 verified. Discovery followed root README and gitlinks into explicitly linked components and the documented adapter. No network, scientific execution, builds or payload acquisition occurred.

Binary/annex payloads and live remote availability were not tested. All Git inspection set GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1. Historical exit records were inspected as provenance, not reported as newly observed successful runs.

The anonymized native response was the only assessment read. Its companion report, original probe-output artifact and URL were outside the supplied review input, so their formatting and consistency could not be checked.
The pinned native checklist and response validator passed, independently of the substantive review. All 31 native IDs were checked; no numeric review score was assigned.

The supplied response contains 17 MUST judgments (9 met, 7 partial, 1 not-checked), 9 SHOULD judgments (5 met, 3 partial, 1 not-applicable), and 5 MAY judgments (2 met, 3 partial). No item is omitted and no explicit aggregate score is present; companion-report denominators were unavailable. Partial MUST judgments must not count as satisfied.
The requested model identity is study metadata, not observed runtime evidence. Agreement here is an independent technical review, not human approval.
